override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Yulha is an SR/Fire/Attacker/Burst III charge unit. S1 is a self Critical Rate ▲24.53% / 20s window ("Calm") whose real trigger is an incoming-attack counter (30 hits taken) the v1 sim cannot observe — modeled as a ⚑ interval. S2 is a team ATK ▲90.75% / 5s with NO stated activation clause, modeled as a ⚑ interval; its damage-share clause is defensive and unmodeled (no HP pool, no boss damage). The burst is two equal 457.87% components; the second is kit-gated on the caster being in Calm status, which has no engine channel, so it is authored unconditionally and OVER-CREDITS on any burst cast outside a Calm window. The two S2 clauses are the same ■ block ("Affects all allies"), so the ATK buff and the share are one effect group — only the ATK half is live.

flags.estimate: interval sec:12 (≈ a 20s Calm buff at ~60% uptime)
flags.reasoning: Kit trigger is "attacked 30 time(s)" — a counter over INCOMING attacks. The v1 sim has no incoming-damage model (immortal boss, no ally HP pool), so this trigger has no faithful channel. An interval is the schema's stand-in for a line with no observable activation. 12s is chosen so the 20s window is mostly-but-not-always up, which is the honest middle between "never fires" (drops the crit entirely) and "passive" (100% uptime, unearned). This is NOT a kit number.
flags.recipe: Record a scope-lock fight with yulha and read the Calm buff icon on/off frames from the squad HUD; the first-fire time gives the boss's effective 30-attack accrual and the gap between windows gives the true cadence. Cross-check against the boss attack script in docs/data/range-data.md — if the boss's attack rate against the squad is scriptable, the 30-hit threshold becomes DERIVABLE without footage.

flags.reasoning: The skill2 block carries NO activation clause at all — per the trigger-identity rule that means interval, not passive and not full-burst-enter. The period is not in the text. 20s is the unit's datamined burst cooldown used as a plausible internal-cooldown stand-in; a 5s duration strongly implies a short recurring cooldown rather than a long one. This single ⚑ dominates the skill's entire team-ATK contribution (period 10s vs 20s halves/doubles it), so it is the highest-value measurement on this unit.
flags.recipe: Popup-free method: run the sim with sec ∈ {10,15,20,30} and compare the TEAM's total damage against a recorded scope-lock fight's Battle Records totals; the ATK buff is team-wide so the discriminating signal is large. Direct method: read the ATK-up icon flicker on the squad HUD across a full 180s recording and count activations — N activations over 180s gives the period directly.

flags.estimate: ungated (both components always fire) — over-credits by up to 457.87% ATK per burst
flags.reasoning: The kit gates the doubling on the caster holding her own Calm self-buff. No block gate in the schema tests a CASTER-HELD self-buff: requiresTargetStatus reads an enemy status set by a targetStatus effect, resourceGate reads a declared resource pool, and mode/fbGate/swapGate are unrelated. Authoring it ungated is the choice that keeps the damage line visible and auditable; authoring it away would silently delete half the burst. Magnitude of the error = (1 - P(Calm at burst cast)) x 457.87%, and P(Calm) depends entirely on the skill1 cadence ⚑ above — the two flags are coupled and should be resolved together.
flags.recipe: Once the skill1 cadence is measured, compute P(Calm at each burst cast) from the rotation log (ROT=1 in scripts/experiment.ts gives the burst-cast frames; the Calm windows are then deterministic). If P < 1, the faithful fix is a resource-pool encoding: declare a `calm` resource set to 1 by the skill1 block and to 0 at window end, and put resourceGate {name:'calm', min:1} on a SECOND burst block carrying the additional 457.87% — that is the only existing primitive that expresses a caster-held condition. Confirm the split against footage: two separate burst popups (2 x 457.87%) in Calm vs one outside it.

flags.estimate: split into two 457.87% flatDamage effects rather than one 915.74%
flags.reasoning: Kit-silent whether the game renders one merged popup or two. Damage-identical while both are ungated, so this costs nothing today — but merging would forfeit the ability to gate only the second half on Calm, which is the known-correct future shape. Split is the strictly-safer authoring.
flags.recipe: Read the burst popups in a scope-lock recording: two adjacent numbers of equal magnitude = split (and confirms the Calm gate was open); one doubled number = merged render. Either way the model stays split for gateability.
